# Bitfab account and connection (Amp, Alpha)

Account and connection management through `bitfab-cli`. Everything here runs in
the terminal.

## Sign in and out

Editor-independent, so these work on Amp directly.

```bash
npx bitfab-cli login
npx bitfab-cli login --force    # re-auth, and clear a stale Studio session
npx bitfab-cli logout
```

`login` opens a browser and returns to the terminal. It short-circuits when
already authenticated, so `--force` is the way to deliberately re-authenticate.

## Session logs

```bash
npx bitfab-cli session-logs status
npx bitfab-cli session-logs enable
npx bitfab-cli session-logs disable
```

Session log collection is off unless enabled. Do not enable it on the user's
behalf. Ask first, and say it uploads session transcripts to Bitfab for
diagnostics.

## Is my setup healthy

```bash
npx bitfab-cli setup --v2 inspect
```

Diagnose (and offer to fix) your tracing setup: auth, what's instrumented, plugin/SDK freshness, replay coverage, trace arrival.

This is the first thing to run for "why are my traces not showing up". Do not
start reading instrumentation code before it has reported.

## Setup modes this skill covers

| Mode | What it does |
|---|---|
| `login` | Authenticate Bitfab for terminal setup. |
| `session-logs` | Opt in or out of session log collection (no login required). |
| `inspect` | Diagnose (and offer to fix) your tracing setup: auth, what's instrumented, plugin/SDK freshness, replay coverage, trace arrival. |
| `switch-org` | Switch which Bitfab org the plugin reads and writes (replaces the local API key). |

Every mode above except `login` and `session-logs` runs through
`npx bitfab-cli setup --v2 <mode>` and needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or another
Claude Agent SDK cloud provider.

## Keeping these skills current

```bash
npx bitfab-cli update --editor amp plugin
```

Reinstalls this skill pack from the published repo, so a newer version replaces
what is installed.

## Not available on Amp in Alpha

`npx bitfab-cli update --editor amp sdk` has no Amp path, because the SDK update
flow launches an editor agent. To check whether the SDK is behind, use
`setup --v2 inspect`, which reports SDK freshness, then upgrade the SDK with the
project's own package manager.
